technical_summary:
Baseline workload: user-facing chat + nightly reconciliation summarization pipeline. Steady-state traffic: 45 QPS (avg), 1.1M tokens/sec total aggregate across 4 regions during peak morning window; peak bursts observed to 380 QPS for short 6–8 minute windows during batch runs.

Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120ms for short-turn chat (<=128 tokens), p99 target <=250ms; summarization batch can be up to 2s but should not block downstream SLA.

Model profile: primary service uses a 13B decoder model quantized to int8 for chat; high-quality summarization uses a 30B float16 variant pinned for certain product flows. Need automatic fallback to a lower-cost 7B variant when Dedicated capacity is degraded.

Sizing assumptions from workshop: a single H100-80GB with optimized kernel and continuous batching handles ~80 concurrent chat QPS for 13B int8 at 128 token length with target tail latency; summarization 30B runs on separate pool with 2xH100 and batch scheduling, estimated throughput ~400 tokens/sec per GPU for summarize workload.

Reserved planning: initial reserved pool recommended: 6x H100-style GPUs (3 for chat pool, 3 for summarization + buffer) with autoscale headroom 2x for burst capacity via burst credits or transient reserved extra. Forecasted committed monthly baseline to meet steady-state + 1.5x safety factor.

Operational controls: continuous prefix caching for common templates, per-route batching windows tuned by latency budgets, smart routing to private fallback model in another region. KV cache retention tuned to token distribution. Observability hooks: token-level latency heatmaps, per-request model variant used, and quota burn reports.

Open technical questions: confirm quantization QA for 30B -> int4 fallback; explicit cold-start behavior for pinned models; validation of prefix cache warmup after autoscale events.
